description: Two zero-fit consistency tests from QOU.MassTheory.AggregatorFamilyExclusions, run against the AME2020 light-nucleus grid. Result: the volume-minus-surface two-parameter family -- the canonical member of the convex class that survived AggregatorConvexityDichotomy -- is EXCLUDED, as is every other correction shape tried, and no pure power law fits either. The surviving aggregator must be convex with an accelerating local exponent, which neither route supplies.
q0_pin: not applicable -- consumes no framework quantity

assertions.name: the volume-minus-surface family c*x - a*x^(2/3) is EXCLUDED on both grid readings -- every (c,a), nothing fitted
every candidate correction shape tried is excluded on both grids (the two-parameter route is empty here)
CONTROL: the degenerate shape psi = x gives det3 = 0, so the test detects genuine degeneracy rather than always firing
no pure power law: the two extracted exponents differ on both grids by more than 0.1
the extracted exponent INCREASES along the grid, i.e. the convexity accelerates rather than settling

scope: (b) for each family as stated -- the invariant is the determinant identity det3_eq_zero_of_realizable and the log-ratio identity powerLaw_log_ratio, both proved in the Lean, not cited. It excludes NOTHING outside those families.
caveats: Test 1 excludes a TWO-parameter family. The full semi-empirical formula also carries Coulomb, asymmetry and pairing terms; on Z = N light nuclei the asymmetry term vanishes, but three points cannot test a three-or-more parameter form at all -- it is UNDERDETERMINED, hence untestable here, NOT excluded here. Do not report these determinants as excluding 'the SEMF'.

The semi-empirical formula is calibrated for A >~ 20 and is known to fail on the light nuclei independently of anything in this framework; 4He is doubly magic. So this exclusion is unsurprising as physics. Its value is that it is now EXACT and zero-fit rather than a remembered fact, and that it removes the obvious candidate before anyone spends a tranche on it.
det3 magnitudes are not comparable across shapes -- only the normalised column is. The psi = x row is a deliberate control: it is column-degenerate with x, so its det3 must vanish, and it does.
A vanishing det3 would mean CONSISTENT WITH, never derived: two parameters on three points leaves one residual, and passing one residual is weak evidence.
